hypothesis: A compile-time-guarded SSE2 scan can skip complete 16-byte ASCII blocks before the existing scalar UTF-8 decoder handles non-ASCII bytes. This may reduce per-byte work on long ASCII spans, but the benefit depends on the official mixed-width input; the first high-bit byte remains for scalar validation. The baseline is valid at 49.623 µs mean, but no candidate speedup is established.
notes: Standalone T2 SIMD-assisted ASCII-run skipping, not T1 whole-buffer validation and not a hybrid. The tree catalog has no T2 results or source diversity yet. The SSE2 path is guarded by __SSE2__; other builds retain scalar scanning. No failed candidate variants are present in the supplied evidence. Await the controller's official n=65536 mixed-width measurement and ASCII/malformed boundary checks.
transformations: Added a compile-time-guarded SSE2 high-bit scan that advances across full 16-byte ASCII blocks only; scalar scanning handles tails and the first block containing a high-bit byte before the unchanged strict decoder validates it.
